Everything You Need To Know About Ink Drops in Disney Lorcana

Deckbuilding will never be the same

By Scott Mines

|@HowlingMines
|

Published Oct 8, 2026

|

14 min read

Copy Link
TCGplayer Series:

It's a very rare thing for a new mechanic to threaten our entire understanding of a trading card game. Once a game moves past the first few booster sets, you tend to find the foundational aspects are baked in and hard to usurp. Disney Lorcana has decided that it doesn't want to play the game that way — anything but. 

Ink drops are about to change the rules of Disney Lorcana and you need to be ready for them. 

If you haven't been following the reveal season leading into Hyperia City, you may not be familiar with what an ink drop is. Ink drops are a new token type that can be created by a menagerie of cards, each of which provides you with a temporary ink. Once you use one it's removed from the game forever. 

This is an absurdly flexible resource. You can stockpile these tokens until it's time to cash in on something huge, accelerate towards a card ahead of time or simply let them fill in for a card you don't want to ink. We saw the power of Sail the Azurite Sea jumping straight to four ink for well over a year and that's the floor on a card like Another Tale to Spin. 

The thing is? That's not all you can do. Hyperia City contains cards that reward you for spending ink drops on them, allowing your new resource to be converted into card draw, additional stats or bonus effects. You'll need to balance these upsides against the power of acceleration and that makes for a wonderful new deckbuilding puzzle. 

I cannot understate how impactful this new mechanic is going to be. Deckbuilding fundamentally changes solely off the existence of ink drops, because you can consistently play on odd numbers/even numbers of ink if you consistently generate ink drops. Mapping out how each color can create ink drops will inform which other cards are playable going forward. This is very emblematic of previous Sapphire deckbuilding to me, but I'm excited to see what it's no longer limited to one color. 

At my count, there are 45 cards in Hyperia City that care about (or create) an ink drop. I want to pinpoint a few of the most impressive ones in each ink and work through what they enable after the release of Hyperia City. 

Amber

We're starting with Amber because it has the least options for ink drops by far. Personally, I think this is deliberate. You can accent Amber with a different ink if you want acceleration, or you can lean into existing tools like Grandmother Willow - Ancient Advisor or Lantern if jumping from two to four is your goal. 

Port Authority - Center Hub is an interesting one. It reads a little awkward to provide the bonus to both players for the work that you're doing, but I haven't forgotten how potent McDuck Manor - Scrooge's Mansion and The Queen's Castle - Mirror Chamber used to be. The stat line on this is very powerful despite it being uninkable.

I'm concerned because it doesn't bridge naturally into Raging Storm, which is the biggest Amber tool I want to accelerate into. If you play Port Authority on turn four, you can move a character into it on turn five to jump to six ink. This only puts you to seven ink on turn six and forces you to have a character in play that'll get swept up by Raging Storm when you play it.

You could play it on turn five and immediately move in a character to fix this? Perhaps you should accelerate into Stitch - Carefree Surfer instead? Unsure. 

In contrast, I think Mickey Mouse - Best in Town is a bit of a beast. It's possible that it fixes the curve issues with Port Authority while providing you with a cheap character to move into it. It may be a hot take, but I think Mickey is much better in a control shell than an aggressive one despite the two lore pips. 

If your opponent is wasting time clearing Mickey, it is buying you the time you want to reach your inevitability. If you're an aggressive deck, you also probably cannot use the ink drops you're generating as well as your opponent. I think there's a lot of power in putting your opponent between a rock and a hard place like this. You either keep questing away... or wreck the opposing counterplay with an opposing Raging Storm. 

Both of these cards have me interested in playing on odds. A Mickey Mouse - Best in Town on turn one allows you to jump to any odd number you like if it's staying alive, while Port Authority is essentially just moving your ink forward a turn. That has me looking at cards like Milo Thatch - Getting His Hands Dirty and Cheshire Cat - Inexplicable as other cards that may make for good haymakers. 

Amethyst 

Amethyst gets significantly more ink drop synergies — eight cards, in fact. However, I expect most of the deckbuilding here to revolve around Madam Mim - Resourceful Trickster.

Mim is the payoff. Immediately drawing two cards on play is quite powerful but drawing additional cards every turn you remove an ink drop leads to an obscene snowball. I believe this is an effect worth building around, so I'm looking for other cards that both accelerate to eight cleanly and generate repeatable ink drops. 

Merlin - Profoundly Curious is far-and-away the obvious stalwart here. In a vacuum, the card is powerful enough on its own, threatening to draw cards as it quests and bridge you directly to six. It also enables the Christmasland scenario of shifting into Merlin - Ink Drop Tinkerer to take you to a theoretical nine ink on turn six. 

That means you're jamming Madam Mim and scoring value from both abilities in the same turn with any one cost card. I'm just expecting this card to see a lot of play either way. 

Inkcaster Skates is very interesting to me. It's one of the few repeatable ways to generate ink drops in the game. Assuming you activate it on turn three when playing it, it'll also allow you to reach eight ink on turn five. That's absolutely perfect for Madam Mim! It's not big or flashy, but I think it has some potential. 

I've also seen a few people talking about Higitus Figitus, but I can't say I'm a believer in this one. Six ink is just so much solely jump your ink drop count. I find myself wishing this card had Sing Together, but frankly that may have been a little bit too good. 

Emerald

Emerald also seems to be quite interested in ink drops, with a hefty nine cards that care about the new mechanic. Interestingly, two of these cards were given epic rarity counterparts, each of which direct you into one of the different directions you can take with Emerald. 

You can jump from two to four like a Bollywood version of Sail the Azurite Sea and Tipo - Growing Son, or you can lean into item synergies and jump up to seven. 

Another Tale to Spin and Molly Cunningham - Remembers to Share are the no-questions-asked accelerants on turn two assuming you don't mind offering an ink drop to your opponent. While this will come back to bite you on occasion, I do think you can build your deck in a way to better abuse the acceleration with a high density of four cost characters. 

Shere Khan - Opportunistic Tycoon and Merlin - Profoundly Curious seem like a wonderful fit to continue up the curve, but maybe something like Cinderella - Ballroom Sensation also tickles your fancy. It seems very easy to daisy-chain from two-to-four-to-six. 

Go Go Tomago - Extreme Tester can achieve the similar thing without providing ink to the opponent but requires them to pick her off in a challenge in order to secure your ink. I think this makes her a better fit in an aggressively slanted deck that can punish with a five-cost card if the opponent tries to slow her down more so than a guaranteed accelerant. This is Business and Kit Cloudkicker - Irrepressible Bear might fit into a shell like that nicely as well. 

The other angle of attack seems to be item focused. Baymax - Lab Assistant is a demon if you can consistently activate it, jumping you straight to a seven-ink turn on turn five. That's a magic number for threats like Milo Thatch - Getting His Hands Dirty or Hades - Infernal Schemer. Even if there isn't quite enough in the chamber just yet, I feel like this card is priced to move. 

Honey Lemon - Testing the Limits isn't the set championship promo card by accident. This is a turbo-fixed spin on Hiram Flaversham - Toymaker, one of the only cards to be banned in the history of Lorcana. The math gets a little weird here because you can play items either before or after Honey Lemon to fuel her ability, changing which numbers you'll want to focus on hitting. Cheap items will make you play smoother on odd numbers, which can be a huge boon for a different item payoff like Ariel - Collector of Oddities... but that's less true if you banished a Blinding Chem Ball. Suddenly, you begin to see all the permutations here. 

I think Bobby Zimuruski - Soundboard Whiz is mostly its own little sidequest. Assuming you have one Bobby and one Leaning Tower of Cheese-a, this can be a quite way to jump up on odd numbers too. Maybe that makes it good enough to enable Baymax, too. 

Ruby 

There's something horrific about the implications of Tadashi Hamada - Making Waves needing to be banished to make ink drops. Does he die again in this card? Can we stop wishing ill on poor Tadashi?! 

Ruby falls on the lower side of ink drop compatibility right now with only five tools to choose from. That being said, I think it may have some of the stronger glue pieces in Meilin Lee - Ecstatic Fan, Pushing Boundaries, and Wasabi - Called into Battle. 

Pushing Boundaries isn't that exciting: it's just yet another way to always jump from two to four ink, which is noteworthy alongside those Emerald cards that were looking to do the same. It just happens to scale a little better into the late game to give you some insulation in an otherwise-problematic challenge. 

Tadashi Hamada is a little more interesting. There's not a ton of ways to secure two ink drops in one burst because it's such a huge jump in resources. This one can't really be ignored because it's questing for three and happily crashes into an opposing character to turbocharge your way up to Madam Mim - Resourceful Trickster or Raging Storm. It's not gigantic, but it's worth thinking about. 

In contrast, I really like Wasabi - Called into Battle. If you're jumping up on even numbers, this is a great play to extend your board and not use up your ink drop, keeping that bottom effect active. If you can do that, this almost plays like a fixed Mulan - Elite Archer: a card that was almost good enough several times between Ursula's Return and Azurite Sea. I'm quite excited to explore what this card can do. 

Sapphire

It shouldn't be a huge surprise that the infamous ink acceleration color gets a decent slice of the ink drop pie. There are eight cards worth watching in Sapphire for all your ink drop shenanigans, helmed by the signpost that is Baymax - Amped Up. 

 

Obviously, the intended play pattern here is to generate two ink drops with Baymax - Lab Assistant, then immediately shift into the gigantic 5/8 character that converts future ink drops into permanent ink. Personally, I think this is very good. It might be "worth building around" levels of good, especially since Emerald Sapphire would give you access to Honey Lemon - Testing the Limits alongside Blinding Chem Ball, Prototype Chem Ball and Honey Lemon - Ingenious Researcher to buy them back. This is clearly an intended archetype. 

There are a few other standouts here though. A Dark Age No More is what I expected Sapphire to get: the ol' double acceleration. This card really has me looking at solid six-cost cards that I can punish the opponent with way ahead of schedule. Demona - Scourge of the Wyvern Clan immediately comes to mind, but even the aforementioned Wasabi - Called into Battle might be a good place to go. 

I'm going to try and brute force Powerline - World's Greatest Rock Star again and figure out the rest later. There's a lot to like here and I expect the card to do some work. 

In contrast to his Ruby counterpart, I think I'm going to find myself hating Wasabi - Future Thinker. We have seen boardwide Ward be disturbingly potent in the past, and Ward as a whole is clearly quite good at the moment — that's why Emerald Sapphire Mouse House is performing so admirably. Adding that effect with a dose of resist thanks to a 5/5 two-lore character feels like it has potential. I just won't be the one exploring it! 

Finally, we have to note Intense Research. If you're spending an ink drop on this card, it's just Visions of the Future. That card was a tried-and-true staple during almost its entire tenure in Core Constructed and I expect the same from Intense Research if ink drops are plentiful. You just have to build your deck as to not use your ink drops on other cards. 

Steel

I saved the big one until last. There are an astounding thirteen cards in Steel that interact with ink drops and some of them are absolute haymakers. We'd be remiss if we didn't begin the discussions with the tiger in the room: Shere Khan - Khan Industries CEO. 

This card is a monster. I have it pegged as one of the best in the set. "New Incentive" enables some backbreaking blowouts alongside characters like Cheshire Cat - Inexplicable, and "Corner the Market" will almost always score you an ink drop on the turn Shere Khan is played because of it. 

That means its removal, acceleration and stats all baked into a single card... which is ridiculous. Curving Shere Khan into Demona - Scourge of the Wyvern Clan is going to be disgusting, but you're going to have to get used to it. 

Khan Transport Delivery is yet another means of "sailing" up to four ink on turn three, but it might be the one that's closest to Sail the Azurite Sea on account of replacing itself. I also think Ink Explosion might be a bit of an underappreciated gem in a world with so many ways to jump to four ink. Consider the following: 

  • Turn 1: Mickey Mouse - Best in Town 
  • Turn 2: Khan Transport Delivery. Quest with Mickey
  • Turn 3: Ink Explosion the first answer to Mickey. Quest with Mickey
  • Turn 4: Prince Charming - Protector of the Realm (or frankly any seven-cost character!) 

It's not always going to come up this way, but I do expect Ink Explosion to remove a threat and refund the ink drop you spend on turn three reasonably often, opening up deckbuilding space for five-cost options like Broadway - Sturdy and Strong too. I'm a big fan of the possibilities here! 

I also think that Marie - Caught in the Act might be the most dangerous ink drop generator of them all. The little kitten not only enables ink from turn two onwards with effects like The Terror that Flaps in the Night, but the card will also be online every time a wayward Strength of a Raging Fire stamps out an opposing character. I think sequencing with Marie is going to be very important, but the card is clearly very strong. 

Closing Thoughts

...and breathe! 

That's a healthy chunk of information to process about ink drops and their various cards. Hopefully the eternal whirring of my mind will help your early deckbuilding attempts with ink drops in mind. 

Be sure to let me know how you get on! If you've got further questions, let me know over at @HowlingMines on X (formerly Twitter) or @howlingmines.com over on Bluesky! Alternatively, give my other work here on TCGplayer a peek if you'd like another slice of everything nice about your favorite game.

But until next time. I've been HowlingMines, you've been amazing!

Stay safe out there — and happy gaming!

Everything We Know About Flesh and Blood's Outbreak

Rangers, Mechanologists and Assassins all blend into a chaotic mix of new heroes for Flesh and Blood's sickest set yet!

By Scott Mines

|@HowlingMines
|

Published Oct 13, 2026

|

12 min read

Copy Link
TCGplayer Series:

Outbreak:  
Noun

Out.break // ˈau̇t-ˌbrāk  

  • a) A sudden or violent increase in activity or currency
  • b) A sudden rise in the incidence of a disease
  • c) A sudden increase in numbers of a harmful organism and especially an insect within a particular area

You didn't think they revealed this card at the very end of World Tour Weekly by accident, did you? Welcome to Outbreak. 

Outbreak is Flesh and Blood's twenty-first mainline set and serves as a continuation of storylines established in Outsiders and Mastery Pack: Assassin. There are even some whispers of Bright Lights in here if you're mechanologically minded.  

An outbreak of disease is plunging the Pits in c̸̡̪̜̈̊͘h̵̛̦̟̒̈́a̶̫͗̌̂ȯ̶̼̺̱̇͊s̷̢̄. Some worship the plague, while others intend to exploit the infected for their own personal gain. Metrix high society is having none of it, employing ruthless exterminators to protect their private interests. Amidst it all, one of the most infamous assassin rangers in all of Rathe is stepping up to eliminate the threats to her home one by one. So many story threads, so little time.  

Outbreak hits shelves on February 12th 2027 and we've got to talk about it. Legend Story Studios just dropped a wonderful product page full of card reveals and sweet as Rathe images. If I wrote about all of those, this article would turn up in like two days, so be sure to go and peek over there too!  

Before you go, let's set up a solid foundation of all things Outbreak. Here's everything we know about Flesh and Blood's sickest set yet! 

More Open Than Ever Before!

Outbreak is a standalone booster set designed for both Limited and Constructed formats. It features six heroes (three Chaos, three dual-class) across the spectrum of Assassin, Ranger and Mechanologist.  

This means chaos in more ways than one. This is six combinations we've never seen before and a real opening of the floodgates for the Chaos talent. If you want to find success within the Pits, you'll need to throw away all pre-conceived notions of these classes... because this isn't like ANYTHING you've seen before.  

But who are they? 

Azalea, Ace of Spades

The infamous fan-favourite ranger has returned to Classic Constructed — she's just a little different than we saw her last. Azalea has picked up her assassin mantle and is filled with determination to save her home from collapse.  

Azalea blends together the evasive arrows of her predecessor with a burst of extension from her assassin side. Much like the Ace in the Hole, you can return cards from your arsenal to the bottom of your deck to place the top card of your deck face up into your arsenal instead. If it has Stealth, it'll gain +1 and Go Again. If it's an arrow, it'll gain Veil (This card cannot be blocked by more than one card of each color)  

This is sweet. It's no secret that Azalea, Ace in the Hole is my least favorite hero ever printed, so my heart fell out of my ass somewhat when I saw her making a return. That said, I think this is a great way to play homage to (and incorporate) some of her original on-hits and evasion in a less polarizing way.  

Similarly, Go Again was often locked to Bolt 'n Shot or Ravenous Rabble, so I'm overjoyed to see her given other options for that angle of attack. I can't wait to find the balance between Stealth attacks and arrows... and hopefully see some Stealth arrows as more cards are revealed. 

Huxley, Racketeer

Assassin Mechanologist eh? How exactly is that going to work?!

Huxley, Racketeer is the underhanded black-market dealer that'll pay for a problem to go away. After all, he's not exactly making that money through anything legal or legitimate. How exactly does a dual-class Mechanologist work given such a focus on Boost in the past?  

By bending the rules, of course.

If you banish an action with Stealth while boosting, you can tap Huxley to turn that card into an instant this turn. This way, you're not upset if you miss your action point from boosting — you can just play the tool you just found instead.  

This hero already has my brain whirling. Zero to Sixty into an Art of Desire: Body? Can I sneak in mark synergies and lean into Mark of the Black Widow and friends? WILL I GET STEALTH MECHANOLOGIST CARDS THAT "GENERATE" AN ACTION POINT BEING BOOSTED AS AN INSTANT?!  

The possibilities feel endless here, which is something highly commendable from what reads like a simplistic design. I'm taking Huxley out for a spin after release 100%.

Min, Genius // Min, Mad

Alright naaaaaaah, this is SICK. What an awesome design with so much depth and forward planning.  

Min's story is a harrowing one. This mechanologist was driven mad after his technology was abused to create ruthless, uncaring Cogwardens. Min has been split between two minds: each with a unique agenda that you'll need to play to when you find yourself on that side of the hero card.  

Min, Genius wants to right his wrongs, inventing new ways to undo the damage he has done. Min, Mad believes that the only solution is total anarchy. What a wicked and wild way to play.  

I wonder what I can do if my cards have no types? That can't all be downside. Perhaps we'll see Chaos Mechanologist cards that provide a bonus if they're not Mechanologist, or vice versa. I love the idea of having to strike a balance between which side of my deck I'm playing to, and the idea of pitchstacking in Min is so exciting. You're telling me I have to track both my cards in deck and which hero I will be at the time? Sign me up.  

Min will also be the beneficiary of the Armory Deck this time around, helping to flesh out the hero identity in more detail. Honestly? The Armory Deck exclusive cards excite me even more. I'm boosting off the opposing deck?! Revere the Copper Idol is such an absurd piece of anti-fatigue for Mechanologists at large and Unstable Plasma Pistol and Madness Spiral are cool as all hell.  

This hero can combine reverse-boost and assassin on-hits to proactively fatigue the opponent too. I'm SO excited. 

Mortimer, Living Virus

Oh no. Bro is not doing okay.  

Mortimer, Living Virus is what happens when you push obsession with science and disease too far. The good doctor is no longer a man: he's a living disease of decay and discourse flowing from his lab into the Pits.  

He is infecting the population both literally and ideologically. To what ends? Well, I'm afraid that's staying REDACTED for now.  

In order to infect your opponent, you'll need to first infect yourself. However, once the great work is complete, you're welcome to cure your own affliction as you see fit. If I'm being honest, the watercolor stylings of this marvel look absurd and I'm desperate to get my hands on one.  

I'm most excited for Mortimer in limited, though. Thanks to the macro for Outbreak (we'll get to that in a bit), there's going to be such a wicked mini game over when to block with which color and why, because Mortimer will be able to confer any disease back towards the opponent. Gimme some packs yesterday.  

As we see more and more effects than taint both players with disease, Mortimer, Living Virus has the potential to flourish. For the sake of the Pits, I'm hoping he fails. 

Vyle, Catalyst of Collapse

Chaos Ranger has my head spinning. We've not had a strong selection of rangers for a hot second, but a hero that goes full-nonsense and loads up both arsenals is a very fun way to spin it.  

Your opponent can always avoid being affected (and turn on the bottom ability) by keeping a face-down arsenal card, but you get to abuse New Horizons in order to still keep an arsenal zone for yourself. God forbid any opponent is playing a Gem into you, which will get stuck forever and permanently turbocharge your arrows.  

The thing is? Keeping Vyle off bonus damage on her arrows requires you to expose yourself to Command and Conquer and Codex of Frailty. They also deny any value they could get from a card like Schism of Chaos. I think that the best part of this ability is the instant-speed window in your own turn, because any opponent relying on a defense reaction from arsenal might suddenly be staring down an arrow that's a little too large for it.  

It's truly hard to put a finger on the pulse of what is possible for Vyle, Catalyst of Collapse, but these small early sequencing puzzles have me excited for her potential. 

a-01, First Cogwarden

Funnily enough, I'm feeling a little validated on this one. My local players asked me how I would design a Mechanologist Ranger just a few months ago, and I almost wrote a-01, First Cogwarden in its entirety. Hilariously, I gave you less of a reward for jumping through the hoops... but one counter seemed fine if the secondary ability was free.  

I think a-01 is the perfect blend of these two classes. The first ability operating at instant speed allows you to keep the opponent guessing as to whether a boosted arrow will become your last action — potentially one they haven't seen you boost away yet! You'll also get to turn some of those arrows into horrific breakpoints thanks to two +1/+1 counters. Remorseless for 7? Keep the change, you filthy animal.  

But I think the most elegant part of this design is that you aren't forced to end on an arrow to make it all work. If you're tight on resources (or simply wanted to end on a different play), you can flip the arrow into your arsenal, then kick off your next turn by granting your juiced-up projectile Go Again instead. I think that sequencing with this hero is going to be very skill testing and I'm all about that noise.  

a-01 – First Cogwarden is probably an early pick for me to explore in Silver Age. I'm very excited to see what this steam machine can do. 

Mortimer's Lab

Outbreak features a format-defining macro for the limited format: Mortimer's Lab.  

This thing has me buzzing like an old fridge.  

Mortimer's Lab gives me some serious Treasure Island vibes in the way that it's going to get you considering almost every attack, but it's also going to get you wracking your brain during deckbuilding. Can you really afford to be eating that many Bloodrot Pox to stack your deck up with reds? Should you block instead of using your arsenal to dodge the risk of Inertia? The possibilities feel endless.  

I love this. I've been a vocal advocate of macro cards for limited formats, but this one adds a lot of the complexity I enjoy to Outbreak. Micro decisions should matter on a macro scale, and Mortimer's Lab is going to have you questioning how to circumvent it from deckbuilding to the end of the top eight. It also plays nicely with Veil: you want to have additional means of blocking evasive attacks, but each card you play to do so makes the next disease less predictable.  

Speaking of diseases...

Exertion

What if you could inflict people with constant doses of Remorseless? Introducing: Exertion.  

Exertion functions like any other disease. It'll plague you for a turn, sucking away your life force for each card played from hand while it's active. This thing is going to be backbreaking in the aggressive mirror matches and really punishes for you hedging against Veil with yellow cards in Limited.  

This disease has wild implications in Constructed and I'm expecting it to be difficult to make. If it isn't? Well, we may have to reassess just how important that arsenal zone is, eh?

Set Breakdown

The set breakdown for Outbreak is as follows:  

  • 274 card set
  • 9 Marvel
  • 5 Legendary
  • 40 Majestic (28 Core, 12 Expansion)
  • 69 Rare
  • 141 Commons
  • 18 Basic 

Silver Age: Outbreak

There are two additional Silver Age decks releasing alongside Outbreak, featuring both of the young-only (as far as I know, anyway!) heroes in the set. Mortimer, Living Virus and a-01, First Cogwarden will each have a $20 USD preconstructed deck that will allow you to get to grips with the hero fresh out of the box!

This is a slam dunk for me. These two heroes have my curiosity piqued already, so I'm happy to have an easy access point towards building both that doubles up as a strong onboarding tool for new players that they appeal to.

World Premiere

The World Premiere for Outbreak will take place between January 29-31 in Philadelphia! I've not had the pleasure of gorging myself at Reading Terminal Market since the 2025 World Championship, so I'm hopeful I'll be making the trip across the pond all over again!

As always, you'll be awarded an exclusive World Premiere promo pack for attending. This time, it contains a marvel variant of Mortimer's Lab and one-of-three randomly selected marvel promo cards. Back Alley Bloodbank, Back Alley Bilebank and Back Alley Plasmabank are all new cards, so you'll have to make sure you peep those! 

Dates You Need To Know

We've got some dates for Outbreak already. If recent event are anything to go by, some of these are going to be hot commodities. Don't miss out on a chance to get involved with this absurdly sweet set.  

  • Spoiler Season Begins: January 16th 2027 
  • World Premiere in Philadelphia: January 29-31 2027 
  • Pre-Release: February 5-7 2027 
  • Silver Age: Outbreak: February 5th 2027 
  • Armory Deck: Min: February 5th 2027 
  • Release Weekend: February 12th 2027 
  • Pro Quest Season Begins: February 13th 2027

Closing Thoughts

Outbreak looks phenomenal. I'm overjoyed to see more sets continuing previous storylines and expanding on the lore of Rathe that we've already come to love. Hybrid mixes of Chaos, Ranger, Assassin and Mechanologist seem like fresh takes on all four of these categories, and I'm itching to get my hands on some cards in order to figure out more. 

What do you think? Let me know over at @HowlingMines on X (formerly Twitter) or @howlingmines.com over on Bluesky! Alternatively, give my other work here on TCGplayer a peek if you'd like another slice of everything nice about your favorite game.

But until next time. I've been HowlingMines, you've been amazing!

Stay safe out there — and happy gaming!

Pokémon|finance

The Biggest Price Spikes in Pokémon This Week - 10/14/2026

Everyone ignored these Prism Star and mid-era cards, until now.

By Corbin Hosler

|@Chosler
|

Published Oct 14, 2026

|

5 min read

Copy Link
TCGplayer Series: Movers and Shakers

It's been said a million times before, but the Pokémon market of 2026 looks absolutely nothing like the Pokémon market of 2006. The world itself is, of course, different in many ways, but there are very few things in life that make some of those changes more obvious than the Pokémon TCG market and what moves cards these days.

It isn't playability, most of the time. It's also not even about the popularity of any given Pokémon, really. Gengar is hyper popular, but there are a million Gengar cards, and most of them are going nowhere in price. It's also not even totally about scarcity. Mega Hyper Rare Mega Darkrai ex is a rarer pull from a Pitch Black pack than the Special Illustration Rare Mega Darkrai ex, but the SIR is slightly more expensive.

What it's really about is attention. Remember the infamous IR Seismitoad out of Black Bolt? Rumors swirled that the card was getting "banned" because of the alleged "666" in the top right corner (it's just squiggly lines), and for two weeks that price hike on the Shinji Konda Toad was all anyone wanted to talk about. But if you were to actually follow that rabbit hole, you'd find there's actually no real source at all for such rumors. What there was was attention, and that's what it really takes to send a card's price moving.

Prism Star Cards Go to the Moon

And that brings us to the big news this week: the drastic jump in price on the Prism Star cards from the quartet of 2018 sets including Celestial Storm, Lost Thunder, Forbidden Light, and Ultra Prism. All of the major Prism Star cards like Latios Prism Star are spiking in price this week, but not because there's a bunch of people who suddenly discovered a new Latios that they want to add to their personal collection.

Instead, it may be simply because this is where the attention is going right now. There's been increased chatter recently about this run of cards, specifically the idea that highly graded copies are particularly difficult to come by—and therefore anyone who does possess a PSA 10 copy will stand to make a lot of money.

Was this based on any actual movement of the graded cards that might suggest pent-up consumer demand? Well, no. The idea is that it has to do with "gem rate"—the rate at which cards receive the highest possible grade. The lower the rate, the harder it is to secure a PSA 10, and the higher the price goes—and we've seen some really silly sales prices on top-end graded cards.

I've done a little bit of research into the topic, and while it does look like this group of cards scores a little lower than the average for a modern-day Special Illustration Rare, I'm not sure that's exactly a reason to go out and buy one. But in what is in some ways a very depressing sentence to write, there are a number of people who look at the Pokémon TCG market with population reports at the forefront of their minds, and this "middle" era of cards is where some people have looked to make money on the next wave. That's the idea anyway.

Well, those future PSA 10s have to come from somewhere, and it seems that a number of buyers are hoping they'll come from TCGplayer seller's stocks. A handful of the Prism Star cards have all jumped in price, led by Latios Prism Star going from $15 to a whopping $75 Market Price in the last week and Celebi Prism Star jumping from $15 to around $60.

Other gainers include Latias Prism Star, which like Celebi went from $15 to over $60, Arceus Prism Star going from $15 to $45, and Jirachi Prism Star going from $25 to $60. Rounding out the winners from that era are Darkrai Prism Star and Giratina Prism Star from Ultra Prism, which both went from around $30 up to closer to $70.

Supply Runs Dry on Mid-Era Cards

Going back further to Aquapolis from 2003, we see a little bit more of the same at work. Since there's been so much attention paid to both ultra-modern Illustration and Special Illustration Rares as well as ultra-vintage staples, there's still almost two decades worth of Pokémon sets in between there that have some very rare cards—even if they don't stand out in quite the same was as a Base Set Charizard or a Blastoise from Scarlet & Violet—151.

But scarcity is the name of the game, and that applies heavily to Houndoom from Aquapolis. The doggo's stock has basically completely run out on TCGplayer. There are listings from earlier this year of played copies that sold around $400, and a Near Mint copy that went for $1,100 in September. But that marked the end of the supply even near that price, and when the next Near Mint copy sold for $1,571 last week, the Market Price officially jumped again.

This Diamond & Pearl promo has been completely bought out in the past month, and the price in that time has gone absolutely bananas. You could have this promo for around $100 as recently as August, but thanks to the recent run we saw a raw Near Mint copy go for a cool $1,000 last week. Again, just a massive jump as the market catches up to the low supply of high-quality copies of these middle-era printings.

In-Print Chase Cards Continue to Drop

It's a very different market than what we're used to, with the big moves on the best IR and SIRs of the day. But reprints continue to lower the price of many recent cards—Ascended Heroes in particular had another down week, with SIR Pikachu ex falling almost $100 to close just under $800 for the first time in many months.

Say what you will about the Pokémon market, there's always something going on! See you next week!

item.description:

The Best-Selling Yu-Gi-Oh Cards From Beyond the Brave

HERO fans are finally getting their support, and buying in droves.

By Zachariah Butler

|

Published Oct 16, 2026

|

5 min read

Copy Link
TCGplayer Series: Bestselling Cards of the Week

Beyond the Brave has been out for a week now, and we've already seen a ton of results from it! Multiple Regional Qualifiers, as well as a slew of online tournaments and a lot of media buzz around it has stirred up plenty of interest in a set that many were overlooking initially.

Between that, the YCS, and the upcoming Forbidden and Limited List that's happening this weekend, sales are a plenty! Let's see what's hot in the set, starting off with a deck that is close to the hearts of many duelists.

The Best-Selling Cards From Beyond the Brave

#10 Destiny HERO – Doom Overlord

Destiny HERO is finally a playable deck outside of Duel Links! The modern Destiny HERO deck is a beast! Destiny HERO - Doom Overlord is a fantastic starter card, loading your grave with key cards and adding your Field Spells to your hand, and having some utility going second as a piece of spot removal. That's a ton of greatness jam packed into one unassuming monster card.

#9 Destiny HERO – Destro-Dogma 

Following the opening act from Destiny HERO - Doom Overlord, Destiny HERO - Destro-Dogma is here to steal the show! Every part of this card has my eyebrows raising up, progressively until they're just gone. Summoned by banishing three Warrior or Darks? Easy work. Then you can set up 2000 damage on the Standby phase? Don't mind if I do! Then, if your foolish opponent is foolish enough to activate a card or effect you get to Fusion Summon by returning materials to the deck? Sure! That just seems silly, and I can't wait to see this slammed onto the table.

#8 Angelechy Seneschal 

The second King in the Angelechy strategy, Angelechy Seneschal fixes some of the problems with the more pure strategy, leveraging your effects into massive swings of board advantage and changing the texture of the entire game. It's absolutely terrifying to see it hit the field, but holy smokes, it's a goodie. This card will be a menace, just watch for the YCS Houston results!

#7 Dark City At Midnight

Infinitely stacking attack stat boosts? We've got that. Searching for any Destiny HERO or a card that mentions a Destiny HERO by name? It does that too! Summoning a Destiny HERO via the effect of Clock Tower Prison on destruction (like your Destroyer Phoenix Enforcer)? Yeah, we checked that box too. Dark City at Midnight does so much it's unbelievable. While it lacks some of the raw utility that other decks may have, depending on what happens over the weekend, this deck could become a very real threat.

#6 Black Skull Dragon, the Archfiend of Unity 

Okay, so here's the thing. This card is really cool, and for some friendly games, it's totally worth playing. That said, so far? It doesn't seem like the most competitively-viable card. The issue is that the summon condition is okay, but you can't use the Quick-Play Spell Card you set the turn you set it. It's just a strictly worse Griffoh. Hopefully though, I'm proven wrong over the weekend because I think it's really neat!

#5 Destiny HERO – Dreadnought Master 

One word. Five letters. One syllable.

PUNCH.

That's what this card does. On summon, Destiny HERO - Dreadnought Master adds two cards to hand that are either Destiny HEROes or mention them. Then its attack is equal to the combined total of all other Destiny HERO monsters on the field or the graveyard, so it gets really big, really fast. This is the final card most duelists will see as their life points disappear faster than good gasoline prices.

#4 Angelechy Strategy Score 

Angelechy is better than ever before, thanks to Angelechy Strategy Score! This card adds any Angelechy Spell or Trap card to your hand, and if it's in the grave you can banish it to return an Angelechy from your backrow to the Extra Deck, then Special Summon it. This card fixes so many problems the deck had, boosting the overall consistency by so much that the deck went from a solid rogue deck to one of the best decks in the format by a mile.

#3 Mediculius the Extraordinary Power Patron

Easily one of the best Link Monsters to be released this year, Mediculius the Extraordinary Power Patron is a behemoth. Forbidden Droplet is one of those cards that we always want to have accessible, and Mediculius is legitimately that on steroids. If it's pointing to two cards it's just unaffected by activated card effects from the opponent, and if it's pointing to three cards it's just a board wipe. That kind of power is extremely rare to come by, and we've seen it already demolishing setups.

#2 Dark Time Wizard 

Mark my words, this card will see top cut playtime soon. It's so good! It not only tutors cards that mention it, but it can absolutely clear an opponent's field. Even if it doesn't clear their field, that's fine. You'll just tribute one of their monsters anyway. That kind of inevitable outcome is terrifying. I fully expect to see Dark Time Wizard getting played to insane levels of success in no time.

#1 Red-Eyes Black Exceed Dragon

Joey Wheeler would be so proud! Red-Eyes Black Exceed Dragon is a behemoth. During the turn any monster was destroyed by Dark Time Wizard, you can simply tribute a monster from either field to summon this big boy. Completely unaffected by opposing activated monster or spell effects, Red-Eyes Black Exceed Dragon then can Special Summon one Level 8 or Lower monster from your hand or grave! Packing 3400 attack points too, this thing is a game ending machine.

That's the bestsellers from Beyond the Brave! Looking past the top 10, we had Swiftwind Panther Warrior at number 11, showing more support for Joey's new toys. Number 12 was Ars Magna the Finite and the Infinite, highlighting the looming threat that the Ars Magna maniacs will pose. Number 13 was Angelechy Brilliant Move, giving even more utility for the already destructive Angelechy deck. Number 14 was Clown Crew Capello, which is surprising to see so low given the fans of the deck gobbling this card up ASAP, and number 15 was Invocation - "Grail", the latest piece for the Invoked deck.

Be sure to watch out for YCS Houston streams - not only are we crowning two more YCS champions, we also get the results of the massive 42-change Forbidden and Limited List update!

item.description:

The 10 Cards Everybody Wants From Riftbound Radiance

Radiant cards worth singing about.

By Drew Knapp

|@FenrirRex
|

Published Oct 19, 2026

|

5 min read

Copy Link
TCGplayer Series:

Riftbound continues to make waves, and I'll be totally honest: up to this point I've been a bit of a fence sitter on the game. I've kept up with the meta out of idle interest, but got precious little play time in personally. League of Legends is an IP that took me awhile to warm up to, but the brand has a silver bullet that's aimed perfectly at me (and other lovers of the K-Pop genre): K/DA. On the extreme off chance you haven't had this earworm enter your brain, allow me to ruin the next few hours of what would've been silence in your head:

Riftbound is printing these very cool, musically themed skins into the game, and they've finally dragged me right in along with that drop. Still, those champions are deserving of one of the top spots on the list here, and I've done my due diligence and want to work my way up to that tier. Let's look at the cards that are grabbing everyone's interest (and what I'll inevitably be picking up as I get properly into the game myself):

#10 Trifarian Captain

Powerful filter effects are big game, and with the loss of Stacked Deck, decks like Miracle Kennen are looking for a critical mass of consistency. Needing to dig for plays like Nocturne - Horrifying is a problem that this helps solve, and it will only get better as the things you're sifting for become more powerful. Now I just need to figure out what kind of gear and units I should be digging for.

#9 Runeblade Anvil

Oh hey, speaking of gear worth digging for. Runeblade Anvil is another tool in the pocket of those miracle-based strategies. The more you can tinker with the top of your deck, the happier you will be, and it can very quickly become downright trivial to beat on the anvil again and again (I'm looking at you Pack of Wonders). Eventually you can accumulate enough card advantage that the opponent just won't be able to compete.

#8 Hush

I'm going to tell you to hush if you're questioning the inclusion here. I definitely recognize that this is more of a sideboard card, but that's exactly why it's here! This is ultimately something of a meta shaper, as it essentially dictates how greedy a player can be during deck building. This is a clear answer to cards that might otherwise be a big problem, and there is even some added irony in Hush being the best answer to itself.

#7 Siren's Song

Not quite Fight or Flight, but i'll definitely do the job. You can't abuse this quite as much, fair, but any kind of counter play to movement shenanigans is going to put in some work. There are all kinds of times that this'll feel particularly rude. Did we get into a big enough dust up that you've finally used all your copies of, say, Punch First? Too bad, nerd, back to base with you!

#6 Blossoming Dreamroot

I love the concept of being able to draw cards just for doing what I want to be doing anyway. Deploy is new, so it's harder to tell if this is as powerful as it looks, but I'm bullish on it even if green decks do not necessarily need the help to get more cards in hand. Calm decks can now reasonably steal Vex – Gloomist's game plan, and Vex can double dip!

#5 Packed Amphitheater (Ultimate)

As a rule, I'm a fan of premium printings, especially if it makes other variants more readily available to players. I absolutely don't expect this to command the same price tag as Baron Nashor, but this represents the chase card of the set for many collectors regardless. I'll admit, I consider it a bit of a weird one altogether, but I would be making a mistake if I didn't highlight that some people will be buying up boxes just for the chance to acquire this.

#4 Heartsteel Overnumbers

Heartsteel returned with a new song prior to the release of Radiance, and it's a banger in its own right. The music video even revealed some of these cards! Fans of the band will be very interested in securing these exclusive treatments, and these get top marks from me.

K/DA may be more my style (and I may just have that 2018 nostalgia helping that along), but you can't deny just how cool these cards look. I'm a big fan of any occasion where you can collect a full set of something worthy of putting on display, and the full band here is exactly that.

#3 Evelyn, Agony's Embrace (Overnumbered)

It will surprise precisely no one that overnumbered legends will be the most coveted pulls from the set. I could stack the whole list with them, but I'm just as interested in the playability of a card as much as its collectibility. Evelyn, Agony's Embrace, is the perfect combination of the two– I'm looking forward to fielding her myself (I do love my demons), and if you tack on the traditional Waifu Tax you have something that will be the premier chase card from Radiance. 

#2 K/DA Showcases

As I said up top, K/DA is the entire reason I'm here, and I guarantee that other new players will be rolling in right behind me. Heartsteel is nice and all, but K/DA is unquestionably THE League of Legends K-Pop band. All of these will be in serious demand, though Ahri is similarly unquestionably the queen when it comes to cards people will be (rightfully) chasing.

Now, notably, these won't be quite as rare as some other showcase cards, but I still wouldn't be surprised if the price tag on these remains consistently impressive. I'm not sure I'm sold on preordering them for $200-$400 with just how common they will actually be in practice, but I'll let the market decide for itself.

#1 Seraphine (Alt)

Going to top off the list with something closer to a personal pick. Yes yes, people are hyped up for the Overnumered variant of Seraphine, but I find the charming, musical theming to the yellow champion to be much more my thing. I'm a sucker for the idol aesthetic as a whole, and I fully expect to see a lot of these on the table.

Where To Find Every MTG Foundations Commander Upgrade Guide

Your journey into Commander begins here.

By TCGplayer Staff

|

Published Oct 19, 2026

|

2 min read

Copy Link
TCGplayer Series: Commander Upgrade

The Magic Foundations Commander decks are some of the most exciting new decks we've had in absolutely ages. Not only are they all mono-colored powerhouses, but they're also cheaper than most preconstructed Commander decks from mainline sets these days, and they make for a great way to get new players into the game. If you've picked one up and you're interested in knowing how to improve it, then we've got you covered. 

Each of these decks come with a simple premise, and for the most part are pretty solid. However, they're also in all beloved Magic archetypes that have plenty of potential upgrade options, and we've got the lowdown on every single one of them. We've also suggested mostly affordable cards as well, so you can keep each one feeling more budget-friendly. 

Calling All Angels

First up is Calling All Angels, which is the mono-white option. This one has Giada, Font of Hope at the front, and is all about angels. Giada helps you get these angels into play earlier because you can tap her for white mana, and each angel comes in with extra +1/+1 counters too. This combines with the overall themes of lifegain and some very strong typal synergies, making it a horrifying deck to play against.

Keen Engineering 

Keen Engineering is all about thopters thanks to Sai, Master Thopterist. Everytime you cast an artifact spell, Sai makes a 1/1 thopter token. In essence, this means that even the least unexciting artifact spells can grant a bit of value to the board. It also means that any ways to boost flying creatures, artifacts, or even thopters specifically, can lead to some massive swings in battle.

Wretched Ranks 

Ghoulcaller Gisa is a mighty commander, as she can spit out zombies at a frightening rate. This deck has some of the best zombie-boosting cards ever printed, including a few cards that desperately needed a reprint as well. You also get some nice sacrifice synergies in there too, turning even a truly dead zombie into a threat with the right set up.

Reign of Dragons 

Lathliss, Queen of Dragons is true to her name, and makes a dragon token every time you play a dragon. Well, technically it's every time a dragon you control enters. She can also boost power to your dragons, which can turn an already scary attack into one that'll hurt your next three games. You do need to figure out the best way to afford all of those expensive dragons, but that's all part of the process.

Tramplesaurus Rex 

Ghalta, Primal Hunger is the most expensive commander in any of these decks, coming in at a whopping 12 mana. She is a 12/12, to be fair, and she also costs less if you've got creatures out. Tramplesaurus Rex is a dinosaur typal deck, and what it lacks in subtlety it more than makes up for in raw power. You're going to be playing some massive creatures, and then just turning them sideways. Doing the math on that kind of thing is for other players — there's a reason "maths is for blockers" is such a popular term in Magic, and it very much applies here.

item.description:
Pokémon|news

Everything We Know About Pokémon TCG: Delta Reign

Mega Rayquaza will descend from the sky on November 6.

By Peter Day

|

Published Oct 9, 2026

|

3 min read

Copy Link
TCGplayer Series:

On November 6, 2026, the Mega Evolution Series of the Pokémon TCG will continue its celebration of the Mega Pokémon from Pokémon Legends: Z-A with the release of its newest expansion: Delta Reign.

Like Chaos Rising and Pitch Black earlier in 2026, Delta Reign will be a regular Pokémon expansion mostly adapted from a single Japanese set—in this case, Storm Emeralda. The reasonable set size of 135+ cards will be good news for fans hoping to pull any of the four versions of Mega Rayquaza ex, the crown jewel of the set for collectors and the most exciting new deck centerpiece for players.

Here's everything we know so far about Mega Evolution—Delta Reign.

When Does Delta Reign Release?

Delta Reign will release on November 6, 2026, with Prerelease events held at local game stores starting on October 24. The cards in Delta Reign will be legal to play two weeks after release, starting on November 20.

All Delta Reign products are expected to be available immediately when the set releases. This includes Booster Boxes, Elite Trainer Boxes, Booster Bundles, and various blister packs. Delta Reign Build & Battle Boxes will be available early, at Prerelease events.

Which Pokémon Are in Delta Reign?

Delta Reign will largely feature international versions of the cards from the Japanese set Storm Emeralda.

The headliner Pokémon of Delta Reign will be Mega Rayquaza ex, the strongest new attacker in the set with three different Secret Rare versions to collect. Besides Mega Rayquaza, Delta Reign features powerful or collectible cards for Raikou, Talonflame, Mega Malamar, Groudon, Kyogre, Growlithe, and Azurill.

While the full set list has yet to be revealed, The Pokémon Company International has confirmed the set will include:

  • Four Mega Evolution Pokémon ex.
  • Six Pokémon ex.
  • Six Stadium cards creating three Legendary Stadiums.
  • 14 Illustration Rare Pokémon.
  • 17 Ultra Rare Pokémon and Trainer cards.
  • Six Special Illustration Rare Pokémon and Supporter cards.

If the full set matches the expected breakdown, the following Pokémon will all have full-art cards in Chaos Rising:

  • Mega Rayquaza
  • Mega Golurk
  • Mega Malamar
  • Mega Golisopod
  • Raikou
  • Groudon
  • Kyogre
  • Kecleon
  • Growlithe
  • Azurill
  • Altaria
  • Inkay
  • Electivire
  • Magmortar
  • Pincurchin
  • Enamorus
  • Masquerain
  • Talonflame
  • Wishiwashi
  • Heat Rotom

What Is a Legendary Stadium?

Delta Reign will introduce a new mechanic to the Pokémon TCG: Legendary Stadiums.

A Legendary Stadium is a powerful Stadium split across two cards. Similar to old Pokémon LEGEND cards like Suicune & Entei LEGEND (Top) and (Bottom), you have to have both halves of a Legendary Stadium in your hand in order to play them as a single game object. If the game rules or a card effect would discard a Legendary Stadium, both halves of the Stadium go to the discard pile.

There are three Legendary Stadiums in Delta Reign, each made of two cards: Legendary Pyroduct, Legendary Trench, and Legendary Summit.

What Are the Chase Cards in Delta Reign?

Mega Rayquaza is unquestionably the star of Delta Reign. The most valuable card in the set will be the Special Illustration Rare version of Mega Rayquaza ex, followed by the Mega Hyper Rare "gold" version of the same card. 

The Japanese version of these cards are currently the most valuable cards in Storm Emeralda by a wide margin.

Rayquaza has a long history of appearing on expensive Pokémon cards, going back to Rayquaza ex from EX Dragon in 2003. While the Sky-High Pokémon had to share the spotlight with Umbreon and other Eeveelutions in Evolving Skies, Delta Reign belongs entirely to Mega Rayquaza ex—no other Pokémon in the set can compete with Rayquaza for name recognition and high-rarity treatments.

What Are the Best Cards in Delta Reign?

Mega Rayquaza ex looks to be the best new attacker coming out of Delta Reign. With built-in Energy acceleration and an attack that scales to KO any opponent, Mega Rayquaza ex has the makings of a serious contender.

It has weaknesses (including a literal Lightning weakness) that have caused it to fall off in the Japanese metagame compared to when it first released. But in the right format, it could still shine.

Talonflame ex's Excited Dive Ability lets players drop it directly into play as long as they have a Colorless Mega Evolution Pokémon ex. Mega Rayquaza ex fits the bill, but most Japanese players have paired Talonflame ex with Mega Kangaskhan ex for a dynamic duo that both hit hard while drawing or searching cards. Its free Retreat Cost helps Talonflame ex keep up in the Basic Box decks that run Latias ex.

The Biggest Yu-Gi-Oh Banlist EVER is Here - What Does It Mean?

Yu-Gi-Oh's largest banlist update EVER has no mercy for long-standing issues.

By Hanko Chow

|

Published Oct 19, 2026

|

14 min read

Copy Link
TCGplayer Series:

YCS Houston brought us 34 newly Forbidden cards as well as the eight newly Limited cards and even Sky Striker Mobilize - Engage! moving onto the Semi-Limited list. There's a ton of changes, so why did they get banned and what does it mean moving forward?

I'm happy to say that I think they've actually done a great job with this banlist. There will always be something missed but this huge update is greatly appreciated and will hopefully make Advanced very exciting again! They checked off most of the spots on my bingo sheet and hit most of the problematic cards while also taking away a handful of cards that I didn't consider.

The Biggest Yu-Gi-Oh Banlist Ever

I'm Sick of These Mitsurugi Snakes on This Mitsurugi Plane

Before going any further, let's address the cards that players have been using to accumulate a lot of material and then use them to find other cards. One of the biggest and most notable perpetrators of this are the Mitsurugi cards, most specifically Ame no Habakiri no Mitsurugi.

I can't believe it's been over a year and five months since Habakiri came out and it's been one of the most competitive engines since its release. It was a key piece in Ryzeal Mitsurugi or any deck that can play with King of the Feral Imps to search it off Herald of the Arc Light with Synchro decks like Yummy. Presently it's still very accessible thanks to Chaos Origin's Ragged Records of Rites and Skull Archfiend of Chaos, not to mention the recently printed Cyberse Contract Witch. I think everyone's happy to say goodbye to Habakiri and good riddance!

When you can resolve the full one-card Mitsurugi combo uninterrupted, you get access to several bodies from multiple Level 8s, to Level 4s, all of which can turn into almost anything you want. We should be thankful that cards like CupsyYummy Way, Magicians' Souls, Cross-Sheep, Saryuja Skull Dread are all newly forbidden as well. This way, other engines that also generate a ton of bodies can't easily replicate what Mitsurugi was doing too.

One of the biggest design flaws in current Yu-Gi-Oh is sending monsters to the graveyard with accessible Extra Deck cards like Zenna's Deceiving Doll Maidens. If you've been in this game long enough, you know that every past version of a Foolish Burial effect that you can easily summon from your Extra Deck has been banned. Lavalval Chain, Beatrice, Lady of the Eternal, Curious, the Lightsworn Dominion - all of them have been banned and Zenna quickly followed suit despite its recent release in Chaos Origins.

Aerial Eater also got a ban, perhaps as a way of preventing the Fiendsmith package from bridging into Rituals thanks to sending Skull Archfiend of Chaos. I'm honestly a bit confused at this decision since they didn't ban Berfomet the Mythical King of Phantom Beasts as it does relatively the same thing and is somewhat easy to summon. Perhaps I'm missing some additional context for this.

Overall, generic card effects that can send anything while also being very easy to access have all been banned, but this time, they're also including the Extra Deck tools that reborn said monsters. Number 60: Dugares the Timeless has been one of the biggest culprits to this as it not only is used for such combos, but it's also just helpful at getting you faster card advantage on turn one since your next Draw Phase might not even matter. Charmer Quartet in Bloom is receiving a similar ban too. It was an important tool at protecting those monsters from specifically Super Polymerization or maybe Super Duper Polymerization since they were both getting popular. Cross-Sheep also fits in this category since it does reborn any Level 4 or lower after you summon a Fusion monster underneath it. Perhaps they missed Selene, Queen of the Master Magicians, but with Magicians' Souls newly banned, it may not be a problem in the near future.

No More FTKS, Floodgates or Hand Loops!

What do players do when they can get anything they want? Well, most players went straight to floodgates when they're uninterrupted or established some negation beforehand, but of course there are also FTKs and hand loops. There were a ton of different variations to these combos like how Power Patron was supposed to summon Superdreadnought Rail Cannon Gustav Max four times since they have enough Level 10s to do so. That combo won't be viable now thanks to it's new limitation without ruining Superdreadnought Rail Cannon Gustav Rocket's potential.

When the new Angelechy cards were first revealed for Beyond the Brave, players quickly figured out how to abuse Angelechy Destrier by giving the opponent a copy of Beelze of the Diabolic Dragons through the effect of Mind Castlin. Once your opponent activates something or you forced them to, the Destrier will inflict 500 damage and then the Beelze will trigger, which creates a loop until they lose all their life points. It's surprising that you can even do this under the strict conditions of only being able to summon Light and Dark Synchros after using Angelechy Opposition or Angelechy Strategy Score. Lukcily for us, banned Beelze of the Diabolic Dragons right away!

Speaking of FTKs, Perfectron Hydradrive Dragon is this new Rank 5 that's coming out in next month's Magnificent Maestros. It was very quickly limited in the OCG after its release so it shouldn't be surprising to see them pre-emptively limiting it before it's officially released in the TCG. If your deck can spam out a ton of bodies to summon multiple Link monsters while also having access to a card like Black Garden, Perfectron Hydradrive Dragon can easily wipe out the opponent's life points since you can actually use a copy of itself to Link Summon for another. With no once per turn clause on its burn effect or summoning conditions, this was definitely going to be a monster to deal with if left at full power. The upcoming Toon cards were also hit for similar reasons. Since Perfect Toon World and Funny Dark Rabbit are so easily accessible and can lead to a lot, they limited the current Toon search Spells to avoid a potential Tier 0 format. Toon Bookmark and Toon Table of Contents are limited for now and we'll see how consistent the new Toon deck is once it's officially released.

Outside of FTKs, the latest banlist targeted effects that take away cards from the opponent's hand. One of which is the classic XX-Saber Gottoms, which can be easy to summon thanks to Ars Magna the Finite and the Infinite and any Level 1 Tuner. There were probably X-Saber combos that could lead to multiple discards from Gottoms thanks to the recently unbanned M-X-Saber Invoker and the X-Saber support from the Legendary Modern Decks, so I'm glad that it's taken care of alongside the classic Trishula, Dragon of the Ice Barrier. I'm not exactly sure why Trishula is banned now but this card has always been powerful on turn one or for breaking boards so perhaps it's time to freeze it for another decade alongside PSY-Framelord Omega and the newly banned Elfnote Tinia. I wonder if they'll ever address Sillva, Warlord of Dark World? Maybe if people somehow randomly decided to make Dark World popular again while fighting off Bystials.

What other cards can instantly win the game that aren't a burn FTK or a hand loop combo? Floodgates! Power Patrons could not only choose to summon Gustav Max multiple times, they could also actually assemble the Amorphage monsters to lock the opponent out of the game since Pendulums can be easily accessed thanks to cards like Beyond the Pendulum and Exceed the Pendulum! Therefore, Amorphage Sloth and Amorphage Goliath received a banned. I'm surprised that Amorphage Lechery escaped, but I'm sure that players will substitute with Amorphage Pride, even though it's a lot weaker.

The Amorphage lock was also supported by the infamous Number 41: Bagooska the Terribly Tired Tapir, which just turned nine years old on this day exactly! Players were forced to draw The Winged Dragon of Ra - Sphere Mode or Lava Golem or go fish. Bagooska has always been a meta-relevant threat since its release, and while it may have fallen off for a while when everyone was using a Link Summoning strategy, now that non-Link summoning strategies are rising in popularity, Bagooska may have overstayed its welcome. It was one of the few cards that's banned in OCG and even Master Duel while somehow roaming free in the TCG. Now that it's banned, perhaps certain endboards like Lunalights, Ryzeal or something like Salamangreat can be easier to deal with.

Spell cards are one of the best ways to break boards or just play the game in general when you're going second, but it really sucked when players could easily search and summon cards like Spell Canceller, Secret Village of the Spellcasters, Naturia Beast and Anti-Spell Fragrance. Having all of these banned will hopefully let players express themselves more and navigate the opponent's end board with ease. Maybe Dark Ruler No More can be viable again!

Anti-Spell Fragrance in particular was not only a problem when you can just drew it, but it was even more annoying when a card like Pharaonic Advent searched for it or any other powerful Continuous Trap like Gozen Match, Rivalry of Warlords and There Can Be Only One. Even though they did ban Magicians' Souls as the main way for players to access Pharaonic Advent, banning the Advent itself is probably also necessary in case other Continuous Traps are too powerful.

Removing End Board Pieces!

Instantly winning on the first turn isn't just about performing an FTK combo or finding that auto-win floodgate, it's about making sure you can stop all six of your opponent's possible cards while also fighting against possible hand traps. That being said, they finally decided to ban the popular Extra Deck cards that resemble a negate. These cards will be joining historic cards like Borreload Savage Dragon, Baronne de Fleur and Apollousa, Bow of the Goddess.

Starting off, there's Azamina Ilia Silvia, the easiest omni-negate to summon since the Sinful Spoil cards are so easy to search thanks to Diabellstar the Black Witch and WANTED: Seeker of Sinful Spoils. This package is super rewarding thanks to the draw one effect of the WANTED poster which you can also search for if you're missing a body via Azamina Mu Rcielago. I'm very happy they're finally addressing this package but I think there's still potential for Diabellstar since you can do so much with her and Dark Magician of Destruction. Even without Magicians' Souls, this package is worth looking into when deck building.

Speaking of Dark Magician of Destruction, the go-to card to search for off it or Dark Magical Curtain is The Gaze of Timaeus to give instant access to Red-Eyes Dark Dragoon. Surprisingly, this boss monster can be very difficult to deal with if your strategy requires you to target the monster to threaten it, which means it can single-handedly win games by itself. This card has been historically a threat whenever a deck can play with it so I'm glad it's finally reached it's end here in the TCG.

Whenever I think of Fiendsmiths, I think of D/D/D Wave High King Caesar. Sure, you could just summon Fiendsmith's Desirae and equip it with Fiendsmith's Sequence to make it untargetable, but it's still vulnerable to single moment negate. D/D/D Wave High King Caesar on the other hand can potentially stop two Special Summon effects or lose out to a one-for-one trade. D/D/D Wave High King Caesar's existence also made Nibiru, the Primal Being a lot weaker since any two Level 6 Fiends can threaten it. Now that Skull Archfiend of Chaos exists, you can not only easily summon it but also recycle it to make Caesar again every turn. Now that Caesar is finally getting banned, we can dust off the Nibirus and try playing with them again!

Varudras, the Final Bringer of the End Times and Crystal Wing Synchro Dragon also protected newer combo decks like Power Patron and Elfnotes, Now, they're both banned, forcing players to search for other ways to protect their combos. Number 90: Galaxy-Eyes Photon Lord is definitely a card that players are eyeing since the new Ars Magna cards can make it pretty often.

I'm a little bit surprised that F.A. Dawn Dragster actually made the cut, but this card has been on the radar ever since Destrudo the Lost Dragon's Frisson was released since it was so easy to summon, especially with Elfnotes. It's a bit of a shame that Crystrons are losing this end board piece, but they still have Cyber Dragon Infinity at least.

Other Important Bans!

I might be exaggerating a bit, but I think everyone feels the same way about Called by the Grave, Triple Tactics Talent and even Crossout Designator. Now players will only have Ash Blossom & Joyous Spring to help fend off opposing Mulcharmys and players won't have to "play around" Triple Tactics Talent and get to use their monster interruptions during the Main Phase fearlessly. These cards being banned is going to be huge for players who like resolving their hand traps.

Speaking of hand traps, Droll & Lock Bird is not getting banned... yet. It might be getting the Dimension Shifter treatment where they're now Limiting the card to see how often players can win with it. Depending on how the meta goes, maybe it could stay legal, maybe it could get banned. I have a feeling that Droll & Lock Bird's days are numbered and it'll be banned before next year.

Griffoh is another monster that can be considered as a hand trap since it can actually set the new Spell Shattering Sword and use it right away! This tech was actually popular at YCS Houston since it's one of the best ways to interact against the Angelechy deck. I was actually going to pick up a set after YCS Houston but I won't be needing to now since they're limiting it. I wonder if you can actually substitute the other missing copies with Kuriboh - Multiply! even if you aren't actually playing the Light and Darkness Ritual deck.

Lastly, they're putting a lot of restrictions for the Branded strategy by outright banning Albion the Branded Dragon. This card is extremely popular due to the fact that any deck can use it with the The Fallen & The Virtuous package. Now players may need to find other substitutes like The Dragon that Devours the Dogma or Titaniklad the Ash Dragon with Dogmatika Ecclesia, the Virtuous to keep using The Fallen & The Virtuous as a destructive engine every other turn. They're also limiting Branded in High Spirits and Branded Opening for some reason. I'm not sure if that's a big deal or not but it'll probably slightly lower the consistency of the Despia Branded deck. I'm sure Branded is still a functioning deck, but losing Albion the Branded Dragon is definitely going to lower the resources and endboard of the deck by a lot.

Oops, I guess I lied, or maybe Konami did, because nobody expected there to be a Semi-Limited card on the banlist since it was never mentioned in the earlier announcement. For some reason though, perhaps in part to Ryan Yu's 18-0 win at the NAWCQ, Sky Striker Mobilize - Engage! is Semi-Limited. Perhaps it's to match with the OCG since they also have Engage at two copies instead of three. I'm sure this doesn't really hurt the deck that much, but it will definitely lower the statistics on how often you can "Engage into Engage."

Closing Thoughts

This covers all 34 newly forbidden cards as well as the eight newly Limited cards and what happened to Engage. I'm super excited to build a new deck and actually go play a local Advanced tournament, and I hope many others feel the same way.

I'm sure the current decks like Elfnote and Light and Darkness Ritual are still viable with the new changes, so we probably need to be aware of that. Angelechy is probably the next go-to bandwagon deck since it seemed to be pretty successful at the YCS even without the Beelze of the Diabolic Dragons FTK. Hopefully these changes are for the better and we can actually have fun playing Advanced until the next broken thing to complain about. Will Mulcharmys be resolving or are they going to be the next big issue? Why are Vanity's Fiend and Vanity's Ruler still legal? Cards like Mistaken Arrest or Different Dimension Ground and Silent Graveyard are difficult to play against. Are Catapult Turtle and Blaze Fenix, the Burning Bombardment Bird FTKs real? Find out next time on the Yu-Gi-Oh TCG banlist update!
